description:
In today's Daily Fix:
Disney has outlined its plans to push further into the gaming space, listing several "billion-dollar" IPs including Marvel Strike Force and Kingdom Hearts. The latter is surprising considering the series has only three main games, and its dozen or so spinoffs are scattered among several platforms. Disney is expected to make a Kingdom Hearts 4 announcement at this weekends' D23 fan expo. In other news, Netflix has shutdown developer Night School, the makers of the cult hits Oxenfree and Oxenfree 2. Their last released project was Unhinged for Netflix. And finally, we take a look at some of the biggest game releases in the coming week.
title: Kingdom Hearts Is a Billion-Dollar Franchises, According to Disney - IGN Daily Fix

author: IGN
description:
Madden NFL 27 reviewed by Jason Fanelli on PlayStation 5, also available on Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and PC.

Madden NFL 27 sports another year of great on-field action, including an improved catching mechanic that works really well once you get the timing down. It’s also made a few improvements to its key modes, such as Franchise's Persona engine and the new catching system. There are still some rough patches that would occasionally frustrate me, like the Combine in Superstar mode, or fail to hold my interest, like Ultimate Team's "same old same old" feeling. None of those are distracting enough to drag the overall package down too far. Like a seasoned veteran, Madden is still waiting for that big breakout season, but it continues to move the needle in ways that matter year after year.
title: Madden NFL 27 Review

author: IGN
description:
Grand Theft Auto 2 legacy review by Luke Reilly. Reviewed on PC and PlayStation.

"Playing Grand Theft Auto 2 again in 2026, I’ve definitely found myself with a stronger appreciation for its technical improvements over the original. Certainly much greater than I gave it credit for back as a teenager in 1999. The driving is better, the shooting is better – and those are important and welcome gains. However, I just cannot muster any true enthusiasm for its retro-futuristic setting. I don’t know that I’d go so far as to call it aggravating but, in the words of the king of rock and roll, it definitely ain’t satisfactioning me."
title: Grand Theft Auto 2 Legacy Review – Revisiting the Retro-Futuristic Sequel in 2026
